html:
The Peramangk are an Aboriginal Australian people whose lands cover the Adelaide Hills, the northern Fleurieu Peninsula and country west of the Murray River in South Australia.

Their neighbours were the Kaurna on the Adelaide plains, the Ngarrindjeri of the lower Murray and the Ngadjuri to the north. The ranges gave them forest game, and they came down to trade and meet with the Kaurna.

The colony of South Australia founded Adelaide in 1836, and settlers moved into the hills within a few years. German Lutheran families founded Hahndorf in 1839. Farming and clearing broke up Peramangk life quickly, and much of what is known of them comes from scattered settler records.
sum: The Peramangk are an Aboriginal Australian people whose lands cover the Adelaide Hills, the northern Fleurieu Peninsula and country west of the Murray River in South Australia.
